Brand identity and product design

Shop
Clarity at every step.

A calm, professional identity for a retail video review workspace. Built around clear evidence, visible system health and considered human decisions.

Design direction 1.0 · 17 November 2026 · Product name: Shop

The symbol

An abstract S uses open framing and rounded geometry to connect the name with observation and continuity. It stays simple enough to recognize at small sizes.

The wordmark

Capital S, lowercase hop. A substantial sans serif gives the product a clear, approachable enterprise character. Keep the supplied lettering and proportions together.

The personality

Clear, composed and useful. Quiet navigation, purposeful colour and contextual information support review work without making the interface feel alarmist.

Logo usage

Placement and scale

Use the supplied horizontal lockup on white or a light neutral surface. Reserve clear space of at least one quarter of the symbol width. Start at a visible mark height of 24px on desktop; verify legibility at the actual exported size.

On dark navigation, place this primary lockup on a small white surface. A white reversed variant and a separately refined app icon are future production variants; they are not included in this PNG concept.

Keep it consistent

Preserve aspect ratio. Do not stretch, rotate, recolour letter by letter, add effects or place the logo over busy footage. Do not use the teal symbol itself to indicate an error or pending incident.

The supplied logo is a 2172 × 724 transparent PNG. It is a raster asset, not an editable vector master. Use the exact tokens below for interface implementation.

Navy for structure. Teal for action.

Let neutral surfaces carry most of the interface. Keep brand accents deliberate and reserve status colours for their meaning.

Typography and components

A consistent rhythm

Review with context.

Use Inter for the product interface, with system-ui as fallback. Use tabular figures for times and operational counts. Self-host approved font files for the local product; this offline guide uses the fonts available on the device.

Official Inter family and licence information

Body and controls 14–16px / 400–500
Supporting caption 12–13px / 400
Body line height 1.5–1.65

Spacing: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64px.
Panels: 12px radius. Controls: 8px radius.
Primary controls: at least 44px high as a design target.

Desktop product concept

A workspace for decisions

Persistent navigation, a scannable review queue and contextual evidence in one place. The strongest emphasis belongs to the selected event and the next deliberate action.

Illustrative UI concept. Counts, footage and camera states are fictional. This is a static visual, not a functioning monitoring application. Exact layout, contrast and wording must be verified in the implemented interface.

Clear navigation

Overview, Review queue, Cameras, Reports and Settings. Keep the active destination visible. On smaller displays, use a labelled navigation drawer rather than unexplained icons.

Context before outcome

Show source, time, visible observation, evidence quality and before/after context. Keep unsupported conclusions and guilt scores out of the interface.

Honest system health

Always show disconnected cameras, processing gaps and unavailable evidence. “No pending events” is different from “Camera offline”.

UX specification

The review flow

1

Find the event. Filter by camera, time and review state. Preserve filters and scroll position when returning from an event.

2

Understand the context. Open footage with visible pre-event and post-event time. Display partial visibility and source gaps alongside the observation.

3

Choose an outcome. Benign, Needs more context or Inconclusive. Start with no outcome selected. The production form should give these choices equal visual weight, then enable a single Save review action.

4

Save deliberately. Show the saved outcome, time and reviewer. Offer a correction that appends to review history; do not silently overwrite the earlier decision.

5

Continue efficiently. Offer Next event after saving. Never advance while evidence is still loading or a draft note would be lost.

Language principle: say “Needs review”, “Partial view” and “Item became obscured”. Do not present “Theft confirmed”, “Shoplifter detected” or a probability of guilt derived from pose.

States and accessible behaviour

Every state has a useful response

Loading: use a stable skeleton and say what is loading.
Empty queue: show source health and last update.
No results: show a Clear filters action.
Offline camera: show last frame time and recovery route.
Expired evidence: state why playback is unavailable.
Unsaved changes: preserve notes or confirm navigation.

Interaction rules

Use visible keyboard focus, native button semantics, labelled fields and text with every status colour. A review drawer must manage focus and return it to its originating event. Escape closes transient overlays without losing a saved decision.

Respect reduced motion. Use restrained 160ms transitions, no flashing alerts and no automatic sound. On mobile, show list then detail sequentially, preserving a visible Back to queue action. Stack the review controls without obscuring playback.

Validate before shipping

Test the core flow with representative reviewers: find an event, inspect context, save an inconclusive decision, correct a review and recover an offline camera. Measure task completion, errors, evidence interpretation and completion time. Check keyboard-only use, zoom, screen-reader labels and actual rendered contrast. This design has not yet been user-tested.
